## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Anabhiratijātaka* (Ja 185) is a short birth story located in the *Dukanipāta* of the Pali Jātaka collection [Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1879]. Set at Jetavana, the narrative was delivered by the Buddha concerning a young brahmin of Sāvatthī who, despite having mastered the three Vedas and taught many noble and brahmin youths, became mired in household responsibilities and family cares, causing his mind to become agitated and forgetful of his teachings [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879; Anandajoti 2010]. In the narrative of the past, the Bodhisatta instructed him with an admonition comparing an agitated mind to turbid water [Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1879]. The canonical verse opens with the line *Yathodake āvile appasanne* ("Just as in water that is muddy and turbid") [Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1879].
This Jātaka must be distinguished from a homonymous story in the *Ekanipāta*, Ja 65, which also bears the title *Anabhiratijātaka* but begins with the verse *Yathā nadī ca pantho ca* and treats the unfaithfulness of women [Burlingame 1921; Narasu 1907; Fausböll 1877].
Regarding parallels and text reuse, SuttaCentral lists no parallels in other canonical languages, while recording four modern translations across four languages [SuttaCentral]. Automated text analysis by DharmaNexus likewise identifies no significant Pali-internal text reuse and no cross-language matches with a score of 10 or above [DharmaNexus].
